newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OCC reduces assessments for 600 banks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OCC reduces assessments for 600 banks.

text.p: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency said Thursday it will reduce assessments for about 600 banks for an annual savings of about $13 million.
The assessments are paid to the OCC to cover its costs of supervision.
The biggest bank in a multibank holding company would be excluded from the 12 percent reduction, which goes into effect Jan. 1, 1997, the OCC said.
"The evaluations of the largest bank capture the risk of the company in general and reduce the scope of risk evaluations needed for other banks in the company," the bank regulator said.
